questions.question: The D1 flexion pattern of the upper limb consists of:
questions.explanation: D1 flexion: shoulder flexion, adduction, external rotation, supination and wrist/finger flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The D2 flexion pattern of the upper limb consists of:
questions.explanation: D2 flexion moves the arm like drawing a sword: flexion, abduction and external rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The D2 flexion pattern of the lower limb consists of:
questions.explanation: D2 lower limb flexion: hip flexion, abduction and internal rotation with ankle dorsiflexion and eversion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The D1 extension pattern of the upper limb consists of:
questions.explanation: D1 extension is the reverse of D1 flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The D2 extension pattern of the upper limb consists of:
questions.explanation: D2 extension is the reverse of D2 flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The D2 extension pattern of the lower limb consists of:
questions.explanation: D2 lower limb extension is the reverse of D2 flexion (hip extension, adduction, external rotation).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: PNF techniques such as alternating isometrics, rhythmic stabilisation and slow reversal hold are given when the goal is:
questions.explanation: Stabilising reversals and rhythmic stabilisation promote co-contraction and stability.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Agonistic reversals and slow reversal are PNF techniques used when the goal is:
questions.explanation: Reversal techniques train controlled mobility.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For people on beta blockers, which measure should be used to monitor exercise intensity?
questions.explanation: Beta blockers blunt the heart rate response, so RPE is used instead.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On average, a duration of ______ is prescribed for improving cardiovascular endurance.
questions.explanation: The conditioning phase of an aerobic session usually lasts 20-30 minutes.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Warm up and cool down periods should each last about:
questions.explanation: Warm-up and cool-down are typically 5-10 minutes each.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On average, a frequency of ______ is prescribed for improving cardiovascular endurance.
questions.explanation: ACSM recommends 3-5 sessions of aerobic exercise per week.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: As training progresses, which component should be increased first?
questions.explanation: Duration is increased before intensity to reduce injury risk.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In inpatient cardiac rehabilitation, exercise intensity should not exceed:
questions.explanation: Inpatients should stay at or below RPE 12-13.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: An RPE of 13-14 on the Borg 6-20 scale represents exercise at about:
questions.explanation: RPE 12-13 corresponds to about 60-75% of maximum heart rate.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the original Borg 6-20 RPE scale, 7 corresponds to:
questions.explanation: 7 is very, very light.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the original Borg 6-20 RPE scale, 9 corresponds to:
questions.explanation: 9 is very light.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the original Borg 6-20 RPE scale, 11 corresponds to:
questions.explanation: 11 is fairly light.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the original Borg 6-20 RPE scale, 13 corresponds to:
questions.explanation: 13 is somewhat hard.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the original Borg 6-20 RPE scale, 15 corresponds to:
questions.explanation: 15 is hard (heavy).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the original Borg 6-20 RPE scale, 17 corresponds to:
questions.explanation: 17 is very hard.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the original Borg 6-20 RPE scale, 19 corresponds to:
questions.explanation: 19 is very, very hard.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Following strength training, hypertrophy of muscle is observed in about:
questions.explanation: Early gains are neural; visible hypertrophy follows after about 6-8 weeks.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of manual resistance?

options.A: It can apply greater resistance than mechanical resistance
options.B: The resistance can be quantified exactly
options.C: It can be controlled and is safe in early stages of rehabilitation
options.D: The resistance cannot be adjusted through the range

questions.explanation: Manual resistance allows the therapist to adjust load at every point of the range.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the goal is to increase strength, the load should be ______ and repetitions should be ______.
questions.explanation: Strength training uses heavy loads with few repetitions.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the goal is to increase endurance, the load should be ______ and repetitions should be ______.
questions.explanation: Endurance training uses light loads with many repetitions.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) typically begins about 12-24 hours after an unaccustomed exercise session and peaks at about:
questions.explanation: DOMS onset is 12-24 hours after unaccustomed exercise, with peak soreness at about 24-48 (up to 72) hours.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A muscle should be held in the contracted state for at least ______ while doing an isometric contraction.
questions.explanation: Isometric holds of about 6 seconds are recommended for strength gains.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In isokinetic exercise, the torque generated and the angular velocity are ______ related.
questions.explanation: Torque falls as angular velocity rises (force-velocity relationship).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which type of contraction consumes less oxygen and energy stores and is more functional?
questions.explanation: Eccentric contractions are metabolically cheaper for the force produced.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Maximum eccentric contraction produces ______ force compared with maximal concentric contraction.
questions.explanation: Eccentric contractions generate about 20-50 percent more force.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the DeLorme progressive resistance protocol, the first set consists of:
questions.explanation: Set 1 is 50 percent of the 10 RM for ten repetitions.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the DeLorme protocol, the second set consists of:
questions.explanation: Set 2 is 75 percent of the 10 RM for ten repetitions.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the DeLorme protocol, the third set consists of:
questions.explanation: Set 3 is the full 10 RM for ten repetitions.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the DeLorme PRE protocol, the 10 RM progression is made once every:
questions.explanation: The 10 RM is reassessed weekly.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the Oxford technique (regressive resistance exercise), the first set consists of:
questions.explanation: The Oxford (Zinovieff) technique starts with the heaviest load and decreases it with fatigue.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the Oxford technique, the second set consists of:
questions.explanation: The load is reduced to 75 percent for the second set.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the Oxford technique, the third set consists of:
questions.explanation: The load is reduced to 50 percent for the third set.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In which progressive resistive exercise protocol does the load remain constant?
questions.explanation: In McQueen's protocol the training load is held constant for all sets and repetitions.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE regarding muscle strengthening?

options.A: There is an increase in the cross-sectional area of the muscle
options.C: There is an increase in mitochondrial density
options.D: The number of muscle fibres may increase slightly (hyperplasia)

questions.explanation: Resistance training does not increase mitochondrial density; endurance training does.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Detraining effects (loss of strength gains) are seen within about ______ weeks of stopping training.
questions.explanation: Detraining begins within about two weeks.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an effect of strengthening exercise on the cardiovascular system?
questions.explanation: Resistance training tends to lower the resting heart rate.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: To improve bone density, ______ training should be given.
questions.explanation: Weight-bearing resistance work loads bone and stimulates osteoblasts.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Training less than ______ days/week produces no significant change in the aerobic endurance of an individual.
questions.explanation: At least 2-3 days per week are required for aerobic gains.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Cardiorespiratory endurance training effect can be seen when an individual reports ______ on the Borg RPE scale.
questions.explanation: Moderate intensity (RPE 12-14) produces a training effect.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For conditioned people, the ideal duration of a training programme should be:
questions.explanation: ACSM guidelines recommend 20-60 minutes, 3-5 days per week.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is FALSE for endurance training?

options.A: The use of fatty acids increases
options.C: There is a slowing in the accumulation of lactic acid

questions.explanation: Endurance training spares glycogen and uses fatty acids more.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: All of the following are true for exercise-induced asthma (EIA) EXCEPT:

options.B: Nose breathing and reduced intensity reduce EIA
options.C: A humid environment reduces EIA and a dry environment induces it
options.D: It is seen 5-15 minutes after vigorous exercise

questions.explanation: EIA is reversible bronchoconstriction that resolves within about an hour.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The amount of work done in interval training is ______ than in continuous training.
questions.explanation: Rest periods let more total work be done at higher intensity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A stretching force produces which kind of stress on tissue?
questions.explanation: Stretching applies tensile force along the tissue.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: According to the stress-strain curve, functional activity mostly occurs in the:
questions.explanation: Normal activity involves low loads within the toe and elastic regions.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: There is considerable weakening of tissue when it reaches:
questions.explanation: Beyond the ultimate tensile strength the tissue necks and fails.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: ______ refers to permanent deformation that occurs when a low-magnitude force is applied for a long duration in the elastic range.
questions.explanation: Creep is progressive time-dependent deformation under constant load.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When a slow stretch force is applied, which structure fires?
questions.explanation: Slow sustained stretch lets the GTO inhibit the muscle, allowing relaxation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true for manual stretching?

options.A: It can be maintained for a prolonged time
options.B: The stretch force is applied for 15-20 seconds
options.D: The risk of injury is minimal

questions.explanation: Prolonged stretching is a feature of mechanical (low-load) stretching.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true for mechanical stretching?

options.A: It is a high-intensity force of over 50% body weight
options.B: The stretch force can be maintained for 20-30 minutes or hours

questions.explanation: Mechanical stretching uses low-intensity loads for long durations.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For effective stretching of tissue, the stretch force should be sustained (held) for:
questions.explanation: A hold of 30-60 seconds is more effective than shorter holds for muscle lengthening.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With increasing tension in the muscle, the Golgi tendon organ:

options.A: Has no effect on the alpha motor neuron
options.D: Facilitates the gamma motor neuron only

questions.explanation: The GTO (Ib afferent) reflexively inhibits its own muscle (autogenic inhibition).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Balance strategies get activated about ______ ms after the instability is perceived.
questions.explanation: Postural responses begin about 80-100 ms after the perturbation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the perturbation is of low amplitude and slow, which balance strategy is activated?
questions.explanation: Small, slow perturbations are corrected at the ankle.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the ankle strategy, muscles are recruited in which sequence?
questions.explanation: The ankle strategy begins at gastrocnemius or tibialis anterior then proceeds to the thigh and trunk.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the perturbation is of high amplitude and fast, which balance strategy is activated?
questions.explanation: Large, fast perturbations are corrected by flexing at the hip.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In the hip strategy, muscles are recruited in which sequence?
questions.explanation: The hip strategy begins with trunk and hip muscles and spreads distally.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which PNF technique is used in ataxia of cerebellar origin?
questions.explanation: Rhythmic stabilisation improves co-contraction and stability.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a safety strategy used in balance training?

options.D: Keeping the centre of mass high

questions.explanation: Safety strategies lower the COM, widen the BOS, use aids and adapt the environment.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Frenkel's exercises were originally designed for ______ ataxia.
questions.explanation: Frenkel's exercises substitute vision for lost proprioception in tabes dorsalis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Relaxation of muscles in Jacobson's progressive relaxation technique follows which pattern?
questions.explanation: Jacobson's technique starts with the hands and feet and moves proximally.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The relaxation technique of Mitchell is based on the principle of:
questions.explanation: Mitchell's simple relaxation uses reciprocal inhibition: contracting antagonists relaxes the tense muscles.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In aquatic therapy, ______ water temperature is used for high-intensity exercise.
questions.explanation: Cooler water allows heat dissipation during vigorous work.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In aquatic therapy, ______ temperature is used for relaxation, mobility and flexibility.
questions.explanation: Warm water (about 33-36 C) relaxes muscles and eases stiff joints.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the water temperature is more than 37 degrees C, cardiovascular demand:
questions.explanation: Heat loading raises heart rate and cardiac output.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In aquatic exercise, which equipment is used to offer resistance for the upper limb?
questions.explanation: Gloves and paddles increase drag on the upper limb.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In aquatic exercise, which equipment is used to offer resistance for the lower limb?
questions.explanation: Fins and boots increase drag on the legs.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In aquatic exercise, which of the following is NOT a buoyancy-assistive device?
questions.explanation: Boots add weight (resistance) rather than buoyancy.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In aquatic exercise, with an increase in speed of movement, the resistance encountered:
questions.explanation: Drag rises with the square of velocity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In aquatic exercise, with a decrease in speed of movement, the resistance encountered:
questions.explanation: Slower movement meets less drag.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the depth of water increases, the load on the extremities:
questions.explanation: Greater immersion increases buoyancy and unloads the joints.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is a PRECAUTION rather than a contraindication for aquatic therapy?
questions.explanation: Non-swimmers can be treated with supervision and flotation aids.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a precaution for aquatic therapy?
questions.explanation: Severe kidney disease is a contraindication, not just a precaution.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For crutch prescription, the distance is measured from the axilla to a point ______ inches ______ from the heel in supine.
questions.explanation: Crutch length is the axilla to a point about 6 inches lateral to the heel (with the foot at the side).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Pressure from prolonged leaning on the axillary bar of a crutch can damage the:
questions.explanation: Crutch palsy results from compression of the radial nerve and vessels in the axilla.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: While ascending stairs with a cane or crutches, the correct order is:

options.A: The affected leg first, then the sound leg
options.B: The cane together with the affected leg first, followed by the sound leg
options.C: The sound leg first, followed by the cane/crutch together with the affected leg

questions.explanation: Up with the good, down with the bad.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: While descending stairs with a cane or crutches, the correct order is:

options.A: The sound leg first, followed by the cane/crutch together with the affected leg
options.B: The sound leg and the crutches together
options.C: The cane/crutch together with the affected leg first, followed by the sound leg
options.D: The sound leg first, then the affected leg

questions.explanation: The stronger leg lowers the body, so the weak leg and aid go first when descending.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In order to guard the patient while ascending stairs, the therapist should stand ______ the patient's involved side.
questions.explanation: Ascending: stand behind and to the affected side to catch a backward fall.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: While descending stairs, the ideal position of the therapist is:

options.B: In front of the patient and towards the weaker side
options.C: Beside the patient on the stronger side
options.D: At the top of the stairs

questions.explanation: Descending: stand in front, towards the weaker side, to prevent a forward fall.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The height of parallel bars should be adjusted so that the elbows are in about ______ degrees of flexion.
questions.explanation: Bars are set at the level of the greater trochanter with 20-30 degrees of elbow flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For patients with a unilateral problem, the cane/stick should be used on the ______ side.
questions.explanation: The cane in the opposite hand reduces the load on the weak leg and keeps a reciprocal gait.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For congenital dislocation of the hip in an infant, the splint used is the:
questions.explanation: The Pavlik harness holds the hips flexed and abducted to keep the femoral head centred.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A single-bar AFO with a medial T-strap is used to correct:
questions.explanation: A medial T-strap pulls the ankle laterally, correcting valgus deformity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A single-bar AFO with a lateral T-strap is used for:
questions.explanation: A lateral T-strap pulls the ankle medially and corrects a varus foot.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Lateral wedging of the shoe can help in correcting:
questions.explanation: A lateral wedge shifts the load toward the lateral compartment and reduces medial compartment loading.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which shoe modification is used in plantar fasciitis?
questions.explanation: A cushioned heel absorbs shock and relieves the painful heel.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A rearfoot varus post reduces:
questions.explanation: A varus-posted wedge on the medial rearfoot prevents excessive inversion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A rearfoot valgus post reduces:

options.B: Calcaneal eversion and tibial internal rotation

questions.explanation: Valgus posting on the lateral rearfoot controls eversion and its associated internal tibial rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For forefoot valgus, which wedge proves useful?
questions.explanation: Forefoot valgus is posted laterally; forefoot varus is posted medially.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For forefoot varus, which wedge proves useful?
questions.explanation: A medial forefoot post brings the ground up to the elevated first ray.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The anterior stop in an AFO limits:
questions.explanation: An anterior (dorsiflexion) stop blocks excessive dorsiflexion; a posterior (plantar flexion) stop blocks plantar flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The posterior stop in an AFO limits:
questions.explanation: A posterior stop holds the foot from dropping in swing and controls knee flexion at heel strike.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is used to correct club foot?
questions.explanation: The Denis Browne bar holds the feet in corrected positions after manipulation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is used in Legg-Calve-Perthes disease?
questions.explanation: The Toronto orthosis keeps the hips abducted and flexed to contain the femoral head.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which device is used in conditions like tight hip adductors or dysplasia of the hip?
questions.explanation: The Frejka pillow keeps the infant's hips flexed and abducted.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which spinal orthosis is used in compression fractures of the spine?
questions.explanation: The Jewett hyperextension brace limits flexion and relieves anterior vertebral loading.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which cervical orthosis provides minimal control of cervical motion?
questions.explanation: A soft collar mainly reminds the patient to limit movement.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which cervical orthosis provides moderate control of cervical motion?
questions.explanation: Rigid collars and 4-poster braces give moderate restriction.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which cervical orthosis provides maximum control of cervical motion?
questions.explanation: The halo (and Minerva) orthosis gives the most rigid immobilisation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The Milwaukee orthosis is a trunk orthosis designed especially for:
questions.explanation: The Milwaukee brace (CTLSO) is used for idiopathic scoliosis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Milwaukee and Boston orthoses can be used when the scoliosis curve is:
questions.explanation: Bracing is used for progressive curves of 25-40 degrees; larger curves need surgery.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which orthosis controls lumbosacral flexion and extension?
questions.explanation: The Knight spinal orthosis restricts flexion and extension at the lumbosacral level.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The Williams brace is used mainly to:
questions.explanation: Williams flexion exercises and brace reduce lordosis in extension-sensitive back pain.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which wheelchair frame is used for highly active individuals (sports)?
questions.explanation: Ultralight chairs are low in weight and adjustable for athletes.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which wheelchair frame is used when a patient cannot self-propel but has the ability to operate a power-driven mobility device?
questions.explanation: Powered chairs suit patients with enough control to drive them.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which wheelchair frame is used when a patient cannot self-propel and has no ability to operate a power-driven mobility device?
questions.explanation: A Geri chair (recliner) is pushed by an attendant.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following wheelchair frames are used when the patient has the ability to self-propel?

options.D: Standard, hemi-frame and one-hand drive frames

questions.explanation: These are manually propelled chair types.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A tilt-in-space wheelchair can be used for patients who have:
questions.explanation: Tilting redistributes pressure and helps manage extensor spasms.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Consequences of an excessively deep wheelchair seat include:

options.D: Kyphosis, posterior pelvic tilt and compromised circulation behind the knees

questions.explanation: A seat that is too deep presses on the popliteal fossa, so the patient slides forward into a slumped posture.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For an adult, the seat of a wheelchair should be about ______ inches wide.
questions.explanation: Adult seat width is the hip width plus about 2 inches, typically about 18 inches.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For an adult, the seat of a wheelchair should be about ______ inches deep.
questions.explanation: Seat depth is the buttock to popliteal fold distance minus 2 inches, typically about 16 inches.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For an adult, the seat of a wheelchair should be about ______ inches in height.
questions.explanation: Standard seat height is about 20 inches from the floor.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For an adult wheelchair, the overall width from rim to rim should be about:
questions.explanation: Standard wheelchairs are about 25 inches wide.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For an adult wheelchair, the overall length of the wheelchair is about:
questions.explanation: Standard length with footrests is about 42 inches.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For an adult wheelchair, the height from the push handle to the floor is about:
questions.explanation: Push handles are about 36 inches above the floor.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For an adult wheelchair, the height from the armrest to the floor is about:
questions.explanation: Armrest height is about 9 inches above the seat.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: For an adult, the back height of a wheelchair should be about:
questions.explanation: Back height is about 16 inches for standard chairs (lower for athletes).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
